title: Anthropic ships Claude Opus 5 into a crowded frontier-model summer
summary: The release lands the same week Nvidia is reportedly weighing a $250B financing guarantee tied to an OpenAI data center — a reminder that model releases and infrastructure financing are now moving on the same clock.

title: Brussels hits Google with its largest Digital Markets Act fine yet
summary: The €890M penalty — split between search self-preferencing and Play Store steering restrictions — comes with a 60-day compliance clock and pushes Google's cumulative EU liabilities past €10B, a concrete marker of how aggressively the EU is willing to enforce platform rules.

title: China's CXMT jumps 466% on debut, becoming the mainland's most valuable listed company
summary: An $8.6B IPO valuing the DRAM maker near $488B is less a stock story than a supply-chain one: AI-driven memory shortages are now minting new chip giants outside the usual US/Korea/Taiwan axis.

title: NVIDIA frames neural rendering as graphics' next default, not its novelty
summary: SIGGRAPH's keynote pitched DLSS 5 and AI-generated frames as a third category of rendering alongside rasterization and ray tracing — worth tracking for anyone building visual or 3D-heavy products, since the hybrid pipeline is becoming the assumed baseline rather than an add-on.

title: Precision Neuroscience clears FDA review for a wireless brain implant
summary: The clearance puts a third serious contender — alongside Neuralink and Synchron — through US regulatory review, a sign the BCI field is shifting from single-company spectacle to a genuine multi-player race.

title: Scribe Therapeutics goes public on a $129M IPO to fund CRISPR cholesterol trial
summary: Its lead candidate, a PCSK9-targeting gene edit for cardiovascular disease, is already in Phase 1 in Australia — one more data point that CRISPR therapeutics is moving from rare-disease niches into mainstream chronic conditions.

title: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 weights go live, deepening the open-weight bench
summary: Another major Chinese lab releasing open weights narrows the gap between what US developers can self-host and what they'd otherwise pay proprietary API vendors for — a trend with real pricing pressure implications, not just an ideological win for open-source.

title: IMF: global growth holds near 3% despite war and tariff crosscurrents
summary: The Fund's July update projects 3.0% growth for 2026 and 3.4% for 2027, with AI-linked demand lifting economies plugged into the tech supply chain even as energy-importing and conflict-adjacent economies lag — context for planning, not a market call.

title: Oil drops over 5% as US and Iran pause military strikes
summary: Brent fell as much as 7.4% on the de-escalation news, though it's still up more than 50% year-to-date — a reminder that a single diplomatic pause can move energy prices faster than months of production data.

title: EdVisorly raises $13.3M to automate community-college transfer admissions
summary: The Series A backs an AI system, Eddie AI, aimed squarely at back-office admissions workflows rather than classroom tools — a sign edtech investors are chasing institutional efficiency plays as much as student-facing products right now.

title: ASUS debuts a ChromeOS desktop and a USB AI accelerator built for classrooms
summary: The Chromebox 6a and UGen300 accelerator, shown at ISTELive, point to schools getting purpose-built low-cost AI hardware rather than repurposed consumer devices — a small but telling sign of the edtech hardware market maturing.

title: John Locke Institute notifies essay-prize finalists as entries top past years
summary: This year's philosophy and politics prompts lean into questions about determinism, moral responsibility, and the institutions underpinning future societies — a useful barometer of which big questions serious students are actually wrestling with.
